packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this leaf. I did not read packet.json. (One directory listing of the three packet directories was made to learn the image filenames; no other directory was listed.)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
Observations:
- One face, upright, of a narrow parchment strip, about 16 cm wide by the scale bar at the foot of the photograph. Single column, long lines.
- The strip is made of two pieces, or one piece with a horizontal fold/cut: an upper block of 16 full lines, then a 17th line sliced through horizontally (only the upper halves of letters survive), then a lower block of 16 lines with a further cropped line at the very foot.
- Right edge trimmed close: several line ends lose a letter or two. Left margin survives with a narrow blank strip; small dark marks in the left margin (stitch holes or ink marks, not letters as far as I can see).
- Round holes at the right of upper line 3, upper line 14, lower line 3 and lower line 14; a stain over a word in upper line 3 and upper line 5; abrasion across the middle of the last four lines of the lower block.
- No running title, no rubric in a different colour visible, no enlarged painted initial. Sentence openings are marked only by slightly enlarged pen capitals in the text ink (S, Q, C, E, H, I, V, D). No underlining. No interlinear or marginal gloss seen; small superscript abbreviation signs only.
- Script: a formal gothic book/documentary hand, brown ink.
Tentative interpretation (not observation): continuous prose in a single block, with one sentence opening that reads like an address formula at the top; I do not infer more.

Areas selected: the whole face, since it is short. Tiles image-002 to image-006 overlap each other; overlaps are noted and not counted as new text.

TRANSCRIPTION

image-002.jpg (top of the upper block; 7 lines)
image-002 l.1: cōuent(us)? loci eiusdē, Salutē ⁊ orationes in dño sa
image-002 l.2: lutares. Q(ua)q(uam)? [enlarged initial, read as Q or O; written "Oq3" with superscript signs] inmenso doloris vulnere humana
image-002 l.3: p̄cordia sauciant(ur). Cū anima in[stain]vita? a corp(or)aliū [hole]
image-002 l.4: mixtura dissoluitur qualitatū quā cōpaginis iūc
image-002 l.5: turā sola mortis ama[stain: ra?] presentia horrendo infrin
image-002 l.6: git diuortio cūcta mundane cōuersatiōis gaudia
image-002 l.7: auferēs in momēto. Et quis sane dolor uberior

image-003.jpg (9 lines; l.1-2 repeat image-002 l.6-7)
image-003 l.1: git diuortio cūcta mundane cōuersatiōis gaudia   [= image-002 l.6]
image-003 l.2: auferēs in momēto. Et quis sane dolor uberior   [= image-002 l.7]
image-003 l.3: aut que maior afflictio cū hec mors impia
image-003 l.4: om(n)ib(us) creaturis predo vite? uiolent(us) existat nec
image-003 l.5: ingenui sāguinis claritati / nec alti p(ar)cens cul
image-003 l.6: minis maiestati. Hec autē humani generis Ini
image-003 l.7: mica inuidia dyaboli ītroiuit in orbē terrar(um). Illu[trimmed]
image-003 l.8: tam diu regnatura / donec nouissima īimica des
image-003 l.9: truat(ur) / et absorbeatur in victoria Jhu xpi qui su[trimmed]

image-004.jpg (9 lines; l.1-2 repeat image-003 l.8-9)
image-004 l.1: tam diu regnatura / donec nouissima īimica des   [= image-003 l.8]
image-004 l.2: truat(ur) / et absorbeatur in victoria Jhu xpi qui sua? [hole above; last letter at trimmed edge]
image-004 l.3: morte iura mortis potenter infringēs elector(um) su[trimmed; suor(um)?]
image-004 l.4: corp(us) humile reformabit / et configuratū corpor[trimmed]
image-004 l.5: [line cut through horizontally: upper halves of the letters sit on the upper piece, lower halves on the lower piece, slightly offset, so the two pieces join here and no line is missing between them]
               claritatis? s[..]? [word with a descender, g or q]? secū?/sciē? [c. 6-8 minims]b(us)?. vn[..]? tutū?/licet? mors?
               Only the first word (claritatis?) and the last (mors?) are offered with any confidence; the middle is not read.
image-004 l.6: reprobis, quor(um) natiuitas mala uita peior
image-004 l.7: mors pessima triste sit exterminiū Justis ta
image-004 l.8: mē quib(us) viuere xpc est ⁊ mori lucrū coope[hole]r[..]? [cooperetur? - hole and trimmed edge]
image-004 l.9: in bonū. Sed quoniā apud deū ex p(ro)prijs operib(us)

image-005.jpg (9 lines; l.1-2 repeat image-004 l.8-9)
image-005 l.1: mē quib(us) viuere xpc est ⁊ mori lucrū coope[hole]r[..]?   [= image-004 l.8]
image-005 l.2: in bonū. Sed quoniā apud deū ex p(ro)prijs operib(us)   [= image-004 l.9]
image-005 l.3: nullus iustificabit(ur) nisi diuini rigor examinis
image-005 l.4: habundātiori clemētia temp(er)etur. sic proinde di
image-005 l.5: uinā excitando mi(sericor)diam piū sit et salubre p(ro)
image-005 l.6: defūctis exorare.. Vniuersitatē v(est)ram / vos ta   [enlarged V]
image-005 l.7: mē obnixius qui nobis Jure sp(irit)ualis fraternita
image-005 l.8: tis obnoxij tenemini Rogam(us) ⁊ exoram(us) in dño.
image-005 l.9: quatin(us) diuini amoris ītuitu pro dil(e)c(t)o n(ost)ro fr(atr)e

image-006.jpg (foot of the lower block; 8 lines; l.1-2 repeat image-005 l.8-9)
image-006 l.1: tis obnoxij tenemini Rogam(us) ⁊ exoram(us) in dño.   [= image-005 l.8]
image-006 l.2: quatin(us) diuini amoris ītuitu pro dil(e)c(t)o n(ost)ro fr(atr)e   [= image-005 l.9]
image-006 l.3: Joh(ann)e cantore sacerdote mo(na)cho ⁊ p(ro)fesso n(ost)ri mo
image-006 l.4: nasterij predc̄i (predicti) nup(er) iuxta nature? debitū viam   ["nature" abraded, read from faint strokes]
image-006 l.5: vniuerse carnis ingresso ac? alijs? n(ost)ris familia   ["ac alijs" abraded] [hole at right above the line]
image-006 l.6: rib(us) quor(um) no(m)i(n)a vobis a latore? presentiū? presen   [middle abraded]
image-006 l.7: tant(ur). Deū cui p(ro)priū ē miser(er)i dignemini? exorare.   [first letters of "dignemini" abraded]
image-006 l.8: [cut at the foot; only the tops of letters survive] Quatin(us)? [..]am? d[..]? s[...] [rest not read; text continued below the cut]

LIMITATIONS AND NOTES
- All 32 full lines of the face are read; the two cut lines (image-004 l.5 and image-006 l.8) are largely unread. Nothing else on this face was left unread.
- The right edge is trimmed; line-end letters at image-003 l.7 (Illu..), l.9 / image-004 l.2-4 are partly lost and are not supplied.
- The first word of image-002 l.1 (cōuent with a superscript sign) stands at the head of the fragment, so the text began on a lost part above; traces of descenders from a lost line are visible at the top edge of image-002.
- The enlarged initial at image-002 l.2 could be Q or O; I give Q(ua)q(uam)? as a proposal only.
- Tentative interpretation, not observation: the wording (salutation, request "Rogamus et exoramus", a named deceased brother, "a latore presentium") reads as a letter-form text asking prayers for the dead. I do not identify a work, author, date or place.
- Only this face is in the packet; the other face, if written, would need its own images.
- Beyond the rules: to read the two cut lines I made native-resolution crops of image-004.jpg and image-006.jpg into a scratch folder (work/crops-reader/) and viewed those crops. No other file, directory, web source or search tool was used, and packet.json was not read.
